Hi Elaine and Tom —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a concise implementation checklist focused on integrating your prompt sets into Redwood's eval harness and wiring up regression alerts and a traffic-ramp/rollback policy for the initial rollout.

Quick ask: can you confirm the two acceptance criteria below by end of day Thursday so we can lock the first canary window?
- Acceptance criteria A: no critical regressions (>=5% drop in top-1 accuracy on core prompt set) for three consecutive canary runs at 10% traffic.
- Acceptance criteria B: support ticket escalation path (CS -> SRE -> Eng) is acknowledged and the on-call contact provided.

Attachments: acme_promptset_v1.csv (sample prompt canonicalization), eval-harness-integration-guide.md, traffic-ramp-matrix.xlsx

- Nov 18: upload prompt sets and confirm SLOs
- Nov 19: run shepherded evals (dry runs) against staging model variant
- Nov 20: begin 10% canary with regression alerts live; 24–48h observation

Next step: Elaine — can you share the canonical prompt examples and the two redlines we discussed (PII masking + allowed response categories)?

Thanks,

Copying in a quick baseline from the Eval team.

Hi all —

A few concrete recommendations from the eval harness side:
1) Dry-run cadence: run three dry evals against staging at different seedings/times to estimate variance; use median delta when comparing to baseline.
2) Regression alert thresholds: set alert on a sustained delta (not single-run) — we recommend 4% absolute drop sustained across two contiguous runs for an automated warning, 6% for a page to Eng.
3) Canary window: start at 10% traffic for 24h; if stable, move to 25% for 48h before full rollout.
4) Auto-rollback policy: if Eng page condition triggers (>=6% sustained drop) rollback to previous model variant and open retrain ticket; include automatic Bcc to SRE.

I'll attach a short integration snippet to the Drive folder (eval-harness-integration-guide.md) that Dylan and Ben helped with.

-Marissa
